name: Albania
notes: no single official page has all four: the civil protection agency's guide gives 127, 128 and 129, the state audit report 112 and 129

name: Andorra
how: Call 112 for mountain rescue; 118 fire, 116 medical, 110 police.

name: Belarus
notes: the state legal portal states 101 and 112 only; 102 and 103 from gov.uk travel advice only (mchs.gov.by, mvd.gov.by, minzdrav.gov.by and belarus.by could not be fetched)

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
notes: numbers from the Sarajevo Canton civil protection authority; no state or entity page found (msb.gov.ba, fucz.gov.ba and mup.vladars.rs searched or tried)

name: Bulgaria
how: Call 112, or the Mountain Rescue Service (PSS) central post on 0887 100 237.

name: Cyprus
notes: source is a 2015 Ministry of Education circular; gov.cy/police could not be fetched

name: France
notes: no single national mountain rescue body (gendarmerie PGHM and police CRS units, reached via 112); gendarmerie.interieur.gouv.fr could not be fetched

name: Georgia
notes: source is the Georgian National Tourism Administration (a government agency); 112.gov.ge, police.ge and mia.gov.ge could not be fetched

name: Greece
how: Call 112. Hellenic Rescue Team (volunteers): SOS line 2310 310 649, 24/7.
notes: the Fire Service site shows 112 only as a header link; gov.gr, 112.gov.gr, civilprotection.gov.gr and astynomia.gr could not be fetched

name: Hungary
notes: no national mountain rescue body found (hegyimento.hu is empty); only regional volunteer teams

name: Ireland
notes: Mountain Rescue Ireland (mountainrescue.ie) could not be read (HTTP 500, expired certificate), so no rescue service is listed

name: Italy
how: Call 118 or 112 and ask for mountain rescue (CNSAS).

name: North Macedonia
notes: no official national source found for 194 and 192; gov.uk travel advice only. Searched the government, police and crisis management centre sites; the only mountain rescue found is the Red Cross Ohrid centre (regional)

name: Malta
notes: the communications authority's page describes the 112 service; pulizija.gov.mt and gov.mt could not be fetched

name: Norway
how: Call 112 (police) or 113 (ambulance). For mountain rescue call 112: the police call out Røde Kors Hjelpekorps.
notes: 110 (fire) backed only by the Oslo municipality fire service page

name: Romania
how: Call 112, or the Salvamont dispatch on +40 725 826 668.

name: Russia
notes: source is the Moscow city government; mchs.gov.ru could not be fetched

name: Serbia
how: Call 112, or the Mountain Rescue Service of Serbia on 062 46 46 46.

name: Spain
how: Call 112, or 062 (Guardia Civil, which runs mountain rescue).

name: Ukraine
notes: the State Emergency Service (dsns.gov.ua), which runs mountain rescue, could not be fetched

name: United Kingdom
how: Call 999 or 112, ask for Police, then Mountain Rescue.

name: United States
notes: source is a National Park Service page; 911.gov and fcc.gov could not be fetched

name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen
how: Call 112; from a satellite phone call the Governor's officer on call, +47 79 02 12 22.

name: Armenia
notes: the Interior Ministry says 112 replaces 911; no mountain rescue service found

name: Morocco
notes: the Health Ministry states 19 and 15; 177 from gov.uk travel advice only (which also lists 150 and 190); service-public.ma, dgsn.gov.ma and protectioncivile.ma could not be fetched
